- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then overshoot, followed by a sharp drop — suggesting overreaction to recent spikes.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- In periods of rising prices, model underestimates the magnitude of the rise, especially when recent history shows upward momentum.
- When true outcome is below historical mean, model often fails to adjust downward, persisting in high forecasts.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent low prices — model takes longer to recognize and correct downward trends.
- Overshoot after spikes is common: model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, then overcorrects.
- Model underestimates downward trends in late forecast periods — especially when true outcome shows continued decline.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the final 5–10 days of the 30d window, often ignoring recent downward momentum.
- Model fails to capture long-term trend persistence — frequently misjudges whether a trend will continue or reverse.
